A public React portal sends HTTPS requests through a WAF and rate-limited API gateway to a Node.js API. Keycloak uses short-lived signed access tokens, refresh-token rotation, MFA for administrators, strict issuer and audience validation, and server-side tenant authorization on every object lookup. The API uses parameterized queries and schema validation, sends TLS connections to a private PostgreSQL database encrypted at rest, and writes immutable audit logs with sensitive-field redaction. Secrets come from a managed vault. Kubernetes workloads run as non-root with read-only filesystems, dropped capabilities, seccomp, resource limits, health probes, private images verified by admission policy, default-deny ingress and egress NetworkPolicies, dedicated service accounts with token automount disabled, and PodDisruptionBudgets.
